verdict.rationale: Circle documents creating wallets through REST APIs, including user-controlled wallets created per user via an initialization challenge and developer-controlled wallet sets for payouts and treasury. Its key-custody model is also documented: Circle secures keys with MPC or passkeys, and the product line distinguishes custodial wallets from user-controlled ones. Missing for 10: explicit evidence that deposit addresses can be provisioned via the API, detailed custody documentation beyond one-line summaries, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create wallets programmatically — per-customer or per-purpose wallets and deposit addresses provisioned through the API with documented key custody semantics

citations.quote: You don't manage raw private keys. Circle secures keys with MPC or passkeys depending on wallet product; you get APIs to create wallets, sign transactions, and authorize actions.
You integrate using REST APIs or Web and Mobile SDKs (Android and iOS).
Creates a challenge for user initialization and creates one or more wallets.
